reason: Photos already opens when I double-click a picture and I never think about it. Making something else the default means redoing file associations by hand, and I redo that on every Windows reinstall.
why_switch_or_not: The portable zip is the one part I like, because I could try it with no install and no admin rights. But it is packed with things I will never use (editor, 3D models, video, batch rename, screenshot importer), and I want a viewer that only views. Speed numbers on someone else's 1440p screen don't mean much for my phone photos and screenshots, and Photos is fast enough for me.
current_app_pros: It's already there and I never set it up. Double-click opens the picture, it handles phone JPGs, screenshots and HEIC-ish stuff without fuss, and it survives Windows reinstalls without me doing anything.
current_app_pains: Nothing much. It is sometimes slow to open the first picture after a restart, and it wants to push OneDrive and its editing stuff on me, but I live with that.
objection: I would have to tick the formats and press Set default myself, then relearn the shortcuts, for a 0.4.1 app from one person that I would have to set up again after every reinstall. The app doing a hundred things I don't need is the opposite of what I want.
would_change_my_mind: A plain, stripped-down mode that only views, with the usual keys (arrows, Esc, zoom) working the way Photos does, and a one-click way to make it default and keep that after reinstall. Or Photos getting annoying enough that I go looking for something.
